prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1231; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received via first notice of loss. Insured reports a low-speed head-on collision in a parking area. Both vehicles drivable. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness after the impact. Claim file opened and assigned for liability and injury review.

Entry 2: Contacted the insured to confirm the facts of the collision. Insured states the other vehicle crossed into their lane while turning. Photos of both vehicles requested and received. Damage appears consistent with a low-speed impact. Police report not required because no one requested one at the scene.

Entry 3: Claimant is now represented by counsel. All further contact to be directed through the attorney's office. Received a letter of representation and a request for the claimant's medical records and a demand for bodily injury coverage. Diary set to follow up on records in thirty days.

Entry 4: Reviewed the medical records provided by counsel. Diagnosis is whiplash-type cervical strain with muscle spasm. Treatment consists of physical therapy and over-the-counter pain medication. Records note prior chiropractic care for unrelated back pain several years ago. Referred the file to the medical review unit for an independent assessment of causation and treatment reasonableness.

Entry 5: Liability assessment completed. Evidence supports a clear liability position against the other driver's policy. Reserves reviewed and adjusted to reflect the current treatment plan. Settlement evaluation pending receipt of the complete billing statements from the treating provider. Supervisor notified of representation status and open medical review.
